note: The raw PoC bytes are copied unchanged into the JavaScript source buffer.
The fuzzer appends a single NUL after the input, so a truncated UTF-8 sequence near the end still has only limited trailing storage.
The constructed source buffer is evaluated by Hermes and reaches the lexer.
Inside the unterminated string literal, the leading 0xf0 byte is recognized as UTF-8 and sent to the slow decoder.
The lexer delegates decoding to the shared UTF-8 slow path with the current pointer into the source buffer.
For a 4-byte lead byte, the decoder reads the fourth byte solely from the lead-byte class without first proving that four input bytes remain.
The truncated input places from[3] past the meaningful source bytes, producing the ASan stack-buffer-overflow read reported by the fuzzer.
